title: Turkish Kebabs by Region: Adana, Urfa, İskender, Cağ & Beyti Explained
seoTitle: Turkish Kebabs by Region: Adana, Urfa, İskender & Cağ
metaDescription: Turkish kebabs guide explaining Adana vs. Urfa, Bursa's İskender, Erzurum's Cağ kebab, genuine ocakbaşı charcoal grills, and şalgam pairings.
quickAnswer: Turkish kebabs vary sharply by region, meat cut, and fire source. Adana uses spicy hand-minced lamb, Urfa skips hot chilli for milder seasoning, Bursa's İskender layers vertical döner over pide with hot butter and yoghurt, Erzurum's Cağ roasts marinated lamb horizontally over wood, and Beyti wraps charred minced meat in lavash with tomato sauce.
category: Inner Pages — 20 Deep Culinary, Regional Food & Beverage Guides

body.text: A practical turkish kebabs guide starts by discarding the idea that "kebab" means one dish. Across Anatolia, geography dictates pasture, sheep breed, and spice tolerance. Whether you are ordering in Istanbul or travelling inland to the towns where these plates were invented, knowing the regional differences helps you order with confidence.
What is the real difference between spicy hand-minced Adana and milder Urfa kebab?

Both Adana and Urfa kebabs consist of fatty lamb minced by hand with a curved twin-handled cleaver (zırh) rather than an electric grinder, then pressed onto wide flat iron skewers. The core difference is heat: Adana incorporates hot red pepper flakes (pul biber), while Urfa relies on mild, smoky seasoning without fiery chilli.

Because hand-mincing preserves tiny pockets of sheep tail fat (kuyruk yağı), the meat stays juicy over glowing oak charcoal instead of turning dense like a burger patty. The [Turkish Patent and Trademark Office Geographical Indication for Adana Kebabı](https://ci.turkpatent.gov.tr/cografi-isaretler/detay/37930) (Registration No. 65) codifies this exact preparation, specifying male lamb meat, tail fat, salt, and red pepper flakes. As [GoTürkiye's Types of Turkish Kebabs guide](https://goturkiye.com/gastronomy/blog/list-of-the-types-of-turkish-kebabs) explains, Urfa kebab keeps the same skewer technique and juicy structure while letting the flavour of the lamb take centre stage. Beyti kebab, popularised in Istanbul in the mid-twentieth century, takes a similar seasoned minced-meat skewer, wraps it in warm lavash, slices it diagonally, and finishes it with tomato sauce, melted butter, and yoghurt.

body.text: Where did Bursa's İskender and Erzurum's horizontal Cağ kebab originate?

İskender kebab originated in 1867 in Bursa's historic Kayhan Bazaar, where İskender Efendi stood a layered lamb skewer upright beside vertical charcoal embers and served shaved slices over diced pide with hot butter, tomato sauce, and yoghurt. Erzurum's Cağ kebab developed in the northeastern district of Oltu, roasting marinated lamb horizontally over crackling wood flames.

You can still trace Bursa's culinary lineage on [GoTürkiye's Taste Bursa guide](https://goturkiye.com/bursa/taste) or plan a dedicated day trip using our [Bursa destination guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/destinations/bursa). In eastern Anatolia, Oltu Cağ Kebabı holds Geographical Indication Registration No. 127 ([KÜRE Encyclopedia — Oltu Cağ Kebabı](https://kureansiklopedi.com/en/detay/oltu-cag-kebabi-85b26)). Lamb is marinated overnight with onion, black pepper, and yoghurt or milk, stacked onto a heavy horizontal iron rod, and turned slowly over birch or oak wood. Diners are served one or two slender metal skewers (cağ) at a time, eating continuously until they tell the server to stop.
What separates a genuine ocakbaşı charcoal grill from tourist-trap kebab shops?

A genuine ocakbaşı ("fireside") centres on a copper-hooded open charcoal hearth where diners sit around the grill master, watching skewers cook over real oak embers (meşe kömürü). Tourist-trap kebab shops typically hide gas grills behind kitchen walls, display glossy multi-language photo menus outside, and station aggressive street touts along main pedestrian avenues.
Before sitting down for kebabs in Istanbul, Gaziantep, or Bursa, run through a quick five-point check:

items: Smell the smoke: Authentic grills burn hardwood charcoal, producing a clean wood-smoke aroma rather than the acrid smell of gas or lighter fluid.
Check the menu length: Serious ocakbaşı kitchens focus on ten to fifteen meat cuts and five simple salads—not pasta, pizza, and burgers.
Watch the skewers: Proper Adana and Urfa kebabs are pressed onto wide, flat iron blades so the meat holds its shape without falling into the coals.
Look for fresh flatbread: Lavash or tırnak pide should arrive warm from the grill's edge, lightly brushed with meat drippings and red pepper oil.
Verify per-skewer or portion pricing: Confirm upfront whether the listed price covers a full portion or a single skewer (tek şiş), especially for Cağ kebab.

body.text: What traditional drinks (şalgam, ayran) pair best?

Rich, charcoal-grilled lamb calls for acidity and salt to reset the palate, which is why locals pair kebabs with şalgam (fermented purple-carrot and turnip juice) or cold, frothy ayran (yoghurt whisked with chilled water and sea salt). Both cut through sheep tail fat far more effectively than sugary soft drinks.

Şalgam suyu—especially Adana Şalgamı, which received European Union Geographical Indication registration as reported by the [Turkish Patent and Trademark Office](https://www.turkpatent.gov.tr/en/news/adana-salgami)—comes in mild (acısız) or spicy (acılı) versions. Order acısız first if you are sensitive to chilli, as the fermented lactic tang is already bold. For İskender kebab or milder Urfa skewers, house-churned copper-cup ayran (yayık ayranı) with thick foam on top is the classic match.

faq.q: Is authentic Adana kebab made with beef or lamb?
faq.a: Traditional registered Adana kebab uses male lamb meat combined with sheep tail fat (kuyruk yağı) and zero beef, though some Istanbul restaurants offer beef-lamb blends for diners who prefer a milder aroma.

faq.q: What does "zırh kıyması" mean on a Turkish kebab menu?
faq.a: Zırh kıyması means the meat was chopped by hand using a heavy curved cleaver rather than pushed through a mechanical mincer, which keeps natural juices locked inside the meat during grilling.

faq.q: Why is Bursa's İskender kebab served with sizzling butter poured at the table?
faq.a: Pouring hot clarified butter over the shaved döner and toasted pide pieces right before eating adds aroma and keeps the thin meat tender while balancing the cool side of thick yoghurt.

faq.q: How many skewers of Cağ kebab is a normal meal?
faq.a: Most diners eat two to four small cağ skewers per sitting, served one or two at a time with warm lavash, sumac-dressed onions, and roasted green peppers.

faq.q: Can you visit an ocakbaşı if you do not eat lamb?
faq.a: Yes. Nearly all ocakbaşı grills also serve marinated chicken thighs (tavuk şiş), chicken wings (kanat), beef tenderloin (çöp şiş or lokum), and charcoal-roasted aubergines and peppers.
No. Şalgam is a non-alcoholic lacto-fermented beverage made from black carrots, turnip, bulgur flour starter, water, and salt, similar in fermentation style to pickle brine.
